artifacts.summary: Confirms the silent-flag-typo defect in issue-record.sh's agent-facing invocation contract, surveys all call sites and the regression-suite gap, and ranks the three candidate fixes (breadcrumb/distinct-exit-code recommended) against the acceptance criteria.

memory_candidates.content: issue-record.sh's manual argument parser has exactly one non-zero exit code (1) shared by every refusal class (missing field, invalid closed-enum value, malformed JSON, unresolvable task, AND an unrecognized/mistyped flag). Combined with every call site's documented non-fatal invocation form (`>/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "Note: issue recording failed (non-fatal)" >&2`), a mistyped flag in the hand-typed agent-facing template (orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's rendered '## Issue Log' section) is silently indistinguishable from any other failure -- the evidence entry is simply dropped with no signal. All ~20 existing *programmatic* call sites build flags from variables so a typo there is a reproducible code bug, not this intermittent class; the real risk surface is specifically the hand-copied template.

A migration-era 'territory contention' list recorded at task-relocation time (naming other open tasks that declare overlapping file_scope) can go stale quickly: checking the 20 tasks named in task 639's migration provenance against the live specs/state.json found every single one already status:completed. Always re-verify a migration-provenance contention list against current state.json rather than trusting it as still-live -- it is a snapshot at migration time, not a durable fact.
